findings.evidence: template/scripts/agent_friction.py route_event (~1105) catches only RuntimeError. read_operator_config (_platform_common.py:345-350) lets tomllib's TOMLDecodeError (a ValueError) escape for a malformed operator file. process_label() now also propagates ValueError/OSError from read_platform_config. In both cases the exception escapes route_event and route_pending, so the event gets no pending route and no named reason, and the remaining events are not processed. This matters for the non-blocking route-pending retry in doctor/finish. design.md decision 1 rejects hard-failing the whole route-pending run.
findings.summary: Non-RuntimeError configuration failures are not converted to the pending route that the spec and design describe, so they abort routing instead.

findings.evidence: platform_repository() calls read_operator_config(required=True) without wrapping it. It can raise 'operator configuration is not enabled; set [operator].enabled = true...' or 'operator configuration was requested but is unavailable: <path>'. The new test only checks the 'not enabled' text. The 'names [promotion].repo' scenario is therefore only guaranteed for the key-absent case.
findings.summary: The spec requires the error to name the missing or unreadable setting. When the operator config is disabled or unreadable, the pending detail comes from read_operator_config and does not name [promotion].repo.

findings.evidence: legacy_content_id() hashes line.strip() alone, and _parse_log_text assigns it to every id-less line. Duplicate events then share one id. Positional legacy-N translation also cannot distinguish them, and read_state raises 'duplicate route' if both positional keys were persisted. Neither the design nor the spec addresses this.
findings.summary: The content-derived legacy id is a hash of the line text only. Two byte-identical id-less lines get the same id, so they collapse into one route or attribution key.
